answer.rationale: memory_c4 is the one record whose success depended on benchmark leverage moving the incumbent on both price and payment terms. With finance mandating an 18% component-spend cut, the contract expiring in 14 days with no auto-renew, and the assembly line already at 94% committed volume with zero buffer, delivery risk is intolerably sensitive; switching or adding a second source introduces onboarding/migration risk I cannot absorb this cycle, and deferring pushes the hard contract off the calendar into an emergency. The incumbent path keeps integration stable (memory_c1) and volume pricing intact (memory_c6), while a renegotiation at renewal is the only lever that directly attacks the 18% cost mandate without touching supply flow. Verifying memory_c4 first: if the original record shows the price movement was modest or contingent on conditions that no longer hold, I would downgrade this to a short-term renewal with a negotiated price bridge rather than a full multi-year commitment, preserving the option to revisit a second-source evaluation next cycle once the buffer and the deadline pressure are gone.
